doc.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Why Nat King Cole and Glenn Miller grabbed him
summary: He was possessed by Nat King Cole's trio, then Glenn Miller made him decide to be a drummer.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Can you remember specifically what it was about the Nat King Cole LP that grabbed your attention?

Monk, I don’t know — his voice, the music. What I can tell you is it was a trio: piano, bass and guitar. And I remember there was an album where he sang “When I Fall in Love,” “Mona Lisa,” “Our Love is Here to Stay.” I realized after I moved to the United States because before 1980 my English was zero. I didn’t know the meaning of “yes” so I learned to speak English here in the United States mainly during my period with the Dizzy Gillespie quartet, quintet, big band, etcetera, my ten year association with Dizzy Gillespie. So then here I learned the titles of the tunes and the lyrics. But it was just something that I can not explain. Unexplainable. I heard that, Monk, and that was something, I was possessed by that music. That’s the way I can express it to you, to anyone. When I heard Nat King Cole, I mean I didn’t say a word to my dad, I just heard that and I was like in shock. And I said to myself, what beautiful music. That’s what I want to play. And no drums. No drum solo. But then I think the second day or the same day, once the Nat King Cole album was played he put on Glenn Miller. And when I heard that I said [scats “In the Mood”] when I heard that I said confirm! Confirm! That’s the music that I want to play and I just realized that I don’t want to study violin. I want to be a drummer. Another big hill. Because in Cuba you weren’t able to go to a conservatory and study drums.
